newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended narrowly mixed on Tuesday. They rebounded off early lows as moderate bargain-hunting emerged amid lacklustre trade, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark October was two yen down at 1,343 yen.

Private investors, who sold earlier in the day, switched to buying later upon seeing the yen's slip, But private investors' participation was still limited amid uncertainty over the currency market, the traders said.
Spot gold was quoted at $378.65/95 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $378.80/379.30 in New York on Monday.
In the spot gold market, constant producer selling continued to pressure the market.
A dearth of inflationary concerns in the United States and weak physical gold demand in Asia were cited as main reasons behind a recent weaker tone in gold.
"Sentiment in gold remains bearish partly because Asian gold demand slowed down recently. Spot gold could test the next support at $377.0 per ounce in the near future," one trading house trader said.
Other precious metals futures also ended narrowly mixed.
Platinum was off early highs on profit-take selling.
Platinum futures ranged from three yen per gram lower to one yen firmer. Benchmark October ended one yen down at 1,371 yen.
Spot platinum was quoted a tad weaker at $384.25/385.00 per ounce at the Tokyo close on selling by Japanese trade houses in arbitrage trade. Platinum opened at $384.50/385.25.
The benchmark October silver contract was 0.4 yen per 10 grams lower at 178.0 yen. The benchmark October palladium contract was up one yen at 429 yen.
